ceiling_statement: The maximum evidence-provenance and transformation-lineage assurance attainable by any H1-H8 system is PER-STEP RECOMPUTE-AND-COMPARE OVER A COMMITTED PURE-TRANSFORMATION DAG, TOTAL OVER THE RELEASE CLOSURE: every trusted artifact in a release has a lineage chain of steps (input-hash, deterministic-transformation-id, output-hash) whose edges are committed under a domain-separated Merkle root bound inside the signed release identity, such that a zero-trust offline verifier re-executes each declared transformation and compares output bytes, with any artifact lacking a complete chain — or any step failing byte-equality — blocking the release (fail-closed totality). Assurance is bounded exactly by (a) the collision resistance of the commitment hash, (b) the purity/determinism of each declared step, and (c) the AX-04 origin ceiling at the chain's roots; nothing feasible exceeds this.
derivation: Three independent limits pin this ceiling, each model-independent. (1) Information-theoretic: un-committed history is unrecoverable — a verifier can establish facts only about data that was committed at production time; no amount of later computation reconstructs which transformation actually ran if only aggregate endpoints were recorded. Hence per-step commitment is not a design choice but the information-theoretic maximum granularity of verifiable lineage; an aggregate base-hash/result-hash + step-count (B0's consolidation ledger today) provably admits distinct histories with identical aggregates, so it sits strictly below the ceiling. (2) Verification theory: with zero producer trust (H8) the verifier may not accept any declared intermediate — the only operation that converts a lineage CLAIM into lineage KNOWLEDGE is re-executing the step and comparing bytes, which is possible precisely when the step is a pure deterministic function (H5: no wall-clock/RNG/IO in the decision); an impure or nondeterministic step is unverifiable offline in principle, so the ceiling covers exactly the pure-step DAG and honest systems must type anything else as UNKNOWN (H2). Recompute-and-compare is therefore both necessary and sufficient — the same argument that makes AX-13's 'offline verifiability cannot exceed recompute-and-compare' absolute. (3) Completeness is a closure property, not a per-artifact property: 'lineage-complete' means the lineage function is TOTAL over the transitive closure of the release — and totality over a finite committed set is decidable by census, so a fail-closed census gate (H3) attains the maximum; no system can exceed totality. Cost floor: verifying n artifacts with s total steps requires Ω(s) recomputation plus O(s log n) inclusion checks; this is feasible today and optimal up to the log factor without trusted state. The whole construction rests on one cryptographic assumption (SHA-256 collision resistance) plus the AX-04 ceiling at the roots — provenance can never exceed the authenticity of its terminal inputs.
attainment_mechanism: This is B0's leading axis and the seat structure already matches the ceiling shape: source/merkle-authority.lisp is the single Merkle seat implementing the RFC 9162 §2.1.1 profile with 0x00/0x01 domain separation and unbalanced split (verified in-file: leaf = SHA-256(0x00‖bytes), node = SHA-256(0x01‖L‖R), consistency-proof/verify-consistency exported), and source/authority-evidence-replay.lisp already re-runs source→spans→extraction→normalization→graph-text to byte equivalence (recompute-not-assert, H8-conformant). To attain the ceiling: (1) upgrade source/consolidation-proof.lisp from aggregate base/result-hash + step-count to a per-step ledger — each consolidation step commits (hash_before, operation-id + canonical parameters, hash_after), the steps chained and their leaves entered into the merkle-authority.lisp tree; the verifier re-executes each step via the existing pure consolidation engine (source/consolidation-engine.lisp) and compares hashes stepwise; (2) make the census in systems/orchestrator-epistemic/artifact-census.lisp a fail-closed TOTALITY gate over the release closure: enumerate every artifact reachable from the release manifest, require a lineage chain terminating in an AX-04-grounded root for each, and block the release (H3) on any orphan — turning the knowledge-graph provenance invariant of source/knowledge-graph.lisp from declared to enforced; (3) bind the lineage Merkle root into the signed release identity via systems/orchestrator-epistemic/release-spine.lisp (which already re-verifies independently) so lineage is inside what the Ed25519 signature covers, and corpus-level identity stays pinned by source/corpus-fingerprint.lisp; (4) add the offline verifier entry that walks the ledger with zero inputs from the producer beyond committed bytes — pure SBCL + SHA-256/Ed25519 already in the repo, no new dependencies.
b0_gap: Per the B0 map AX-06 row, the gap to the ceiling is narrow but real: (a) the consolidation ledger verifies ONLY aggregate base/result hash + step-count, not the per-step hash chain (source/consolidation-proof.lisp) — exactly the aggregate-vs-per-step distinction the derivation shows is strictly below ceiling; (b) census totality over the release closure is not a blocking gate — lineage completeness is checked where declared, not proven total, and the knowledge-graph provenance invariant is declared rather than enforced; (c) no machine-checked proof that the Lisp Merkle implementation refines the RFC 9162 spec (the profile is asserted in comments and exercised by tests, not proven — part of the AX-21 0/17 proof debt); (d) the chain's roots inherit the AX-04 gap: lineage bottoms out on un-attested government-source.lisp origin bytes until the AX-04 mechanism lands.
lean_obligation: Model the ledger as a DAG: `structure Step where inHash : Digest; op : OpId; outHash : Digest`, with `apply : OpId → Bytes → Bytes` a pure total function (the deterministic transformation semantics) and `hash : Bytes → Digest` collision-resistant (axiom). Define `stepOK (s : Step) : Prop := ∀ b, hash b = s.inHash → hash (apply s.op b) = s.outHash` and `chainOK : LineageChain → Prop` as the transitive per-step conjunction rooted at an AX-04-Grounded input. Prove: (TOTAL) `∀ a ∈ releaseClosure R, ∃ c : LineageChain, endpoint c = a ∧ chainOK c ∧ ∀ s ∈ c, inclusionProof merkleRoot s` — lineage is a total function over the release closure with every step committed under the root that the release signature covers; (CEILING) for any verifier V satisfying H5/H8, `V accepts (a, history h)` implies h's per-step hashes were committed and each recomputation matched — i.e. V's knowledge is bounded above by chainOK, and an aggregate-only ledger admits `h ≠ h'` with identical aggregates (a two-history counterexample lemma, showing aggregate verification is strictly weaker); (REFINE) `∀ leaves, lispMTH leaves = rfc9162MTH leaves` — the implementation refines the RFC profile including the odd-leaf unbalanced split and domain separation.
